risks: GPU probes (nvidia-smi/rocm-smi) may be unavailable or require elevated privileges on this host, leaving GPU/VRAM fields empty and forcing a CPU_HEAVY or REMOTE_GPU_REQUIRED classification rather than a GPU class.
Sustained storage throughput measurement can perturb the host or take long; it must be bounded and read/write-safe to avoid violating the no-mutation boundary.

Usable-VRAM and KV-cache context sizing depend on display/runtime overhead that varies by session; the envelope must be conservative and explicitly labeled as a candidate, not a frozen deployment decision.
Port/firewall enumeration may be incomplete without root, risking an over-optimistic 'usable ports' claim; findings must record the access level used.

The package forbids selecting an inference backend from assumptions, so the CUDA/PyTorch/serving compatibility check must remain a recorded finding only; any drift toward actually installing a stack would be a boundary violation.
steps: Classify as bounded: the deliverables are five report files in the existing work package directory; no new subsystem, no interface change, no code that others depend on. Announce the bounded path and present this short design in chat before touching anything.

Rebaseline and record the exact candidate revision (git SHA/digest of the work package) and the environment manifest (hostname, user, timestamp) that every artifact will be bound to, so T03 stale-revision detection has a reference.

Write the probe scripts first (the RED step): a single inventory collector that shells out to lscpu, free, df, lsblk, nvidia-smi/rocm-smi, docker/podman info, firewall status, and port scans, emitting host_inventory.json, gpu_probe.log, and the raw inputs for the markdown reports. The failing probe is that these five deliverables do not yet exist or are empty.

Run the collector read-only and capture OS/kernel/distro, CPU, RAM, disk/free/filesystem, every GPU with VRAM/driver/CUDA-ROCm/compute mode/topology, Docker/Podman, firewall, virtualization, and usable localhost/LAN ports into host_inventory.json and host_inventory.md.
Measure model-cache capacity and sustained storage behavior (sequential read/write throughput and free-space headroom) and write disk_capacity_report.md.

Compute the capacity envelope for model weights, KV cache, builds, Buzz services, and concurrent agents, and classify the host as HIGH_THROUGHPUT_GPU, SINGLE_GPU_CONSTRAINED, CPU_HEAVY, or REMOTE_GPU_REQUIRED in deployment_profile_candidate.md.

Apply the three mechanical failure-mode controls: derive usable VRAM from nvidia-smi free/used (not total) after display/runtime overhead; cap the recommended context length at what the measured KV-cache budget sustains rather than the model's 262k maximum; and record the CUDA/PyTorch/serving compatibility check as a recorded finding, not an install, since no backend may be selected from assumptions.

Execute the companion test matrix T01-T08 plus at least two real adversarial tests (context-overcommit and total-vs-usable VRAM) by changing runtime/input conditions, capturing command, exit code, timestamp, and candidate revision for each.
Prepare the independent verification packet (frozen obligations, work product, artifact hashes, upstream lock entries, environment manifest, findings) and stop; do not self-accept.
accepted_plan.summary: A read-only host inventory and capacity-envelope work package that is fully satisfiable as written, requiring only probe scripts and five report artifacts with no system mutation.
accepted_plan.test_first: A failing probe asserting that the five mandatory deliverables (host_inventory.json, host_inventory.md, gpu_probe.log, disk_capacity_report.md, deployment_profile_candidate.md) do not exist or are empty in the worktree, plus a RED check that the inventory collector emits no usable-VRAM or sustained-context figure until the read-only probes actually run — establishing the missing-behavior baseline before any report is produced.
